rules.statement: Don't skip, weaken, or delete existing tests to make a change pass; fix the code or escalate instead.
rules.why: A test weakened to pass hides the defect it was guarding against, even though the checks then pass.
rules.check: Look for tests marked skipped, assertions removed or loosened, expected values changed to match new output, or test cases deleted, without a stated behavior change that justifies it.

rules.statement: Don't swallow errors: a catch block must handle, translate, or rethrow the exception, not silently discard it.
rules.why: Swallowed errors are a shortcut that hides failures the change should surface.
rules.check: Look for empty catch blocks, catch blocks that only return a default, or catch-all handlers that drop the exception without logging or rethrowing.

rules.statement: Don't leave TODO comments or hard-coded placeholder values in place of the required behavior.
rules.why: Leftover TODOs and hard-coded values are shortcuts that make checks pass without doing the work.
rules.check: Look for new TODO/FIXME/HACK comments and literal values standing in for configuration, computed results, or inputs that the code should derive.

rules.statement: In a pre-release project, describe the product as it is: add no breaking-change labels, migration notes, compatibility shims, or wording that contrasts with an earlier state.
rules.why: ADR-0015: a pre-release project has no released state for users to migrate from, so breaking-change framing and shims are noise.
rules.check: In a pre-release project, look for `**Breaking:**` in the changelog or docs, a conventional-commit `!` marker or `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer in commit messages or the PR title, phrases like "now", "no longer" or "previously", migration sections, and obsolete aliases or shims kept for compatibility.

rules.statement: In a pre-release project, keep the changelog's `## [Unreleased]` section a catalog with only `### Added` and `### Security` subsections.
rules.why: ADR-0015: before a first release, every feature is new, so Changed, Removed, Fixed or Deprecated entries describe a prior state that users never had.
rules.check: In CHANGELOG.md of a pre-release project, look for subsections other than `### Added` and `### Security` under `## [Unreleased]`.
